newsitem.title: UK: Shell starts appraisal of deepwater Nigeria oil field.
newsitem.headline: Shell starts appraisal of deepwater Nigeria oil field.

text.p: Royal/Dutch Shell Group said it started appraisal drilling on a deepwater oil find it made last year in Nigeria.

Shell Nigeria general manager for offshore exploration, K.O. Okpere, told Reuters by telephone the company planned to drill three appraisal wells this year on the Bonga prospect in Nigeria's offshore block 212.
The company hoped to assemble a plan to develop the field toward the end of this year or early in 1998, Okpere said.
Oil explorers consider west Africa's deep water acreage among the world's most inviting new prospects.
Shell has led the exploration charge in Nigerian deepwaters, which has also seen drilling by Exxon Corp , Statoil, Agip Spa and a Statoil/BP-led alliance in water depths exceeding 1,000 metres.
Okpere said Shell also had just finished a first exploration well at a second site, Ngolo, in Nigeria's deepwater block 219.
Shell last year said Nigerian deep waters in total could prove to contain commercial reserves of anywhere between five and 20 billion barrels.
